hook.text: Gravity storage lifts heavy weights when energy is cheap—then lowers them to generate electricity when it's needed.

buildup.text: Energy Vault stacks concrete blocks using a crane—raising them with surplus power and lowering them to generate.

discovery.text: The physics is simple—potential energy equals mass times gravity times height. More weight and height means more energy.

twist.text: Old mine shafts could serve as gravity storage—lowering weights down deep shafts and winching them back up.

climax.text: Gravity storage has no chemical degradation—it works for decades with minimal maintenance, unlike batteries.

punchline.text: Lift a block, drop a block—gravity stores energy simply.

quiz.question: What is a key advantage of gravity storage over batteries?
